title: Pinelock Media Group
description: The corporate site of the holding company that owns the Verity Ledger and thirty other local news properties, with an investor page, a careers page and no reporters.

blocks.body: Pinelock Media Group is a privately held operator of local media properties. The Group publishes [b]31 properties[/b] across [b]four states[/b] on a single unified publishing platform, reaching approximately 1.9 million monthly unique readers.

The Group was formed in 2009 to acquire and operate community publishing assets in secondary and tertiary markets. Our thesis has not changed since: these markets are durable, underserved by national media, and structurally overbuilt on the cost side. We buy well-regarded local titles, retain the mastheads readers know, and move the work of producing and distributing content onto shared infrastructure.

items: [b]One platform.[/b] All 31 properties publish through the same system, on the same templates, with the same taxonomy. Transition was completed across the portfolio in the fourth quarter of 2024.
[b]Shared services.[/b] Production, scheduling, categorisation, distribution, ad operations, billing and legal-notice compliance are centralised. Properties do not maintain their own stacks.
[b]Local identity, preserved.[/b] Mastheads, property names and legal-notice standing are retained through acquisition. Readers should not need to know who owns a title.
[b]Volume discipline.[/b] Published output per property rose 41% year over year while average cost per published item fell to $2.40.
[b]Nothing stranded.[/b] Where a market cannot support a standalone title, the property is consolidated into a surviving property in the same operating group rather than closed.

blocks.body: Figures as of 30 June 2026 and unaudited. See [url=/investors]Investor Information[/url] for definitions and for the Group's treatment of forward-looking statements.

[b]Pinelock Media Group Announces Portfolio Review[/b]
[i]14 January 2026[/i]

Pinelock Media Group today announced a review of its property portfolio, with the objective of identifying opportunities for further operating efficiency and platform standardisation. The review is expected to conclude in the second half of the fiscal year. The Group does not comment on individual properties.

[b]Kim Redditt Named Senior Vice President, Content Operations[/b]
[i]6 October 2025[/i]

Pinelock Media Group today announced the appointment of Kim Redditt as Senior Vice President, Content Operations, effective immediately. Ms. Redditt joins the Group from a national customer-experience outsourcing provider, where she led a 900-seat delivery organisation.

[b]Pinelock Media Group Completes Platform Transition[/b]
[i]19 November 2024[/i]

Pinelock Media Group today announced that all 31 of its properties are now publishing on the Group's unified platform. The transition, begun in 2018, standardises production workflow, content taxonomy and advertising delivery across the portfolio. Chief Executive Officer Ellis Grandin said the milestone "removes the last of the duplicated cost in this business."
Media inquiries: [b]communications@pinelock-media.com[/b]. Inquiries regarding coverage, corrections or submissions are not handled at this address; see [url=/standards]Content Standards[/url].

[b]Posted[/b] 4 August 2026. [b]Reposted[/b] 2 September 2026. [b]Location[/b] Remote. [b]Reports to[/b] Manager, Content Operations (Central Pod). [b]Compensation[/b] $19.25 to $21.00 per hour, depending on experience.

[b]About the role.[/b] The Content Operations Associate supports the daily publishing cycle across an assigned block of properties. You will work a queue. The queue is the job. Associates are typically assigned 28 to 40 properties and are measured on throughput, hold time and category accuracy.
[b]What you will do[/b]

items: Monitor the publishing queue across assigned properties and clear held items within the 30-minute service level.
Verify category, market and geography tagging on queued items before release.
Apply the correct property template and confirm that the property's standard attribution line has populated.
Process reader submissions received through intake: obituary notices, public notices, event listings, school and youth sports results, and photographs.
Triage items flagged by the automated consistency check and route per the escalation matrix. Do not resolve flagged items independently.
Process correction requests received through the intake form, apply the appropriate correction type, and confirm the correction has posted to the property's corrections page.
Maintain the approved-terms and restricted-terms lists for assigned properties.
Log volume, hold time and exception counts in the daily operations report.

blocks.body: [b]What we are looking for[/b]

items: Associate degree, or equivalent practical experience.
One year in a queue-based production, moderation, transcription or customer-operations environment.
Comfort working at volume. Assigned blocks typically run 600 to 900 published items per property per month.
Strong attention to formatting detail. Most of what we correct is formatting.
Ability to follow a documented process exactly, including when the process appears to produce an odd result. Process questions go to your manager, not into the item.
Prior journalism experience is not required.

blocks.body:
[b]Schedule.[/b] Five days, including one weekend day. Shift assignment is by pod and rotates quarterly. The Central Pod covers the eastern two operating groups and starts at 5:30 a.m.

[b]Equipment.[/b] Laptop and headset provided. Associates are responsible for their own connectivity. A wired connection is required; the platform is not supported over cellular.

[b]Benefits.[/b] Medical, dental and vision after 90 days. 401(k) with a 2% match after one year of service. Accrued paid time off beginning at 11 days annually. Employee assistance program.

[b]To apply.[/b] Applications are accepted only through our applicant tracking system at [url=synth://pinelock.talentroster.synth/]pinelock.talentroster.synth[/url]. Please do not send résumés to Group email addresses or to individual properties; they cannot be entered into the process and will not be acknowledged.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Due to volume, we are unable to respond to every applicant.

items: Remote-first. The Group maintains one office, in Bellhaven, and does not require attendance.
Documented process for everything. If you find something undocumented, that is a ticket and we would like you to file it.
Flat structure. Content Operations is nine people.
Internal mobility. Two of the Group's four operating group leads started in an hourly role.

Pinelock Media Group is privately held and has no publicly traded securities. This page is maintained for the Group's lenders, noteholders and prospective transaction counterparties. Nothing on it is an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any security.

Figures are unaudited and are presented on a management basis. "Published item" means a distinct unit of content released to a property's public site through the Platform, including items released to more than one property. "Cost per published item" is total content operations cost, including allocated platform and licensing cost, divided by published items. It excludes revenue operations, corporate and interest.

items: Platform transition completed across the portfolio in Q4 FY2024. All 31 properties now publish on common infrastructure with a common taxonomy.
Published item volume increased 41% year over year in H1 FY2026 while content operations headcount declined from 14 to 9.
Cost per published item declined for the seventh consecutive quarter.
Reader-submission and correction intake was centralised into a single queue in March 2025, retiring 31 property-level intake paths and the associated telephone lines.
Four sub-scale titles were consolidated into surviving properties in FY2025. Legal-notice standing and the associated statutory revenue were retained in each case.
Two remaining owned buildings were sold and leased back in FY2025 under the Real Estate Optimisation Program. One owned property remains.
Syndicated regional copy is licensed under a flat-rate agreement renewed in January 2026, replacing per-item pricing.

The Group competes for local advertising and reader attention with national platforms, with programmatic inventory generally, and with a growing set of low-cost regional publishing networks, including Meridian Local Network. Competition of this kind is expected to continue to pressure revenue per thousand impressions.

Management's view is that the response to that pressure is cost per item rather than price. The Group has reduced cost per item by 23% over eight quarters and believes there is further room.

This page contains forward-looking statements, including statements regarding portfolio composition, operating cost, published item volume, platform standardisation and the outcome of the portfolio review announced in January 2026. Forward-looking statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties, including changes in advertising demand, changes in search and distribution referral, the availability and cost of licensed content, statutory changes affecting public-notice publication, litigation, and the Group's ability to service its indebtedness. Actual results may differ materially. The Group undertakes no obligation to update any forward-looking statement.

Every property in the Pinelock portfolio publishes under the same standards document. This page is a summary of it. The controlled version is internal.
Items published on the Platform are assembled from a defined source set. Sources outside that set are not admitted.

items: Agendas, packets and minutes published by a governmental body in the property's market.
Public safety dispatch summaries as released by the responsible agency.
Official statements, releases and filings issued by an identified organisation.
Notices, obituaries, listings and results submitted through the Group intake form.
Licensed regional wire copy. The Group licenses county and regional copy from [url=synth://veritywire.press/]Veritywire Press[/url] under a flat-rate agreement.
Material previously published by a Pinelock property.

blocks.body: The last category is the one readers ask about. A property may republish, update or expand an item that originated at another property in the portfolio. Where it does, the item carries the standard attribution line and no separate credit.

Items produced through the Platform carry the property's standard staff designation. Individual attribution is applied only where an identified contributor has supplied original material under a current contributor agreement.

A staff designation is a property attribute. It does not denote an individual and should not be read as one. Designations in use across the portfolio are reviewed annually and are changed from time to time; a change to a designation is not a change to the underlying item and is not treated as a correction.

All items pass an automated consistency check before release. The check compares asserted names, dates, figures and place references against the source document set and against previously published items on the Platform.

Items that fail the check are held and routed to Content Operations. Held items are cleared, corrected or suppressed within the service level. The Group does not publish the pass rate.

Correction requests are accepted through the Group intake form only. The form is linked from the footer of every property site.

Requests received by any other route cannot be entered into the queue and will not be actioned. This includes telephone calls to a property's legal-notice number, correspondence sent by post to a property address of record, comments left on third-party platforms, and messages sent to Group email addresses.

A complete request identifies the property, the item, the specific text at issue and the correct information, with a source. Requests that do not identify a specific item cannot be processed. Requests concerning items published prior to a property's platform transition cannot be processed, as pre-transition archives are not maintained.

Actioned corrections are posted to the property's corrections page. For The Verity Ledger, that page is at [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/corrections]now.verityledger.com/corrections[/url].

items: We do not accept news tips. There is no intake path for an item that is not already in the source set.
We do not arrange interviews, at Group level or at property level.
We do not remove published items at request, except where required by law or by a court of competent jurisdiction.
We do not disclose the composition of the source set for an individual item.
We do not comment on the content of any individual item.

[b]Ellis Grandin[/b] founded Pinelock Media Group in 2009 and has served as Chief Executive Officer since formation. He previously held operating roles in regional directory publishing and in outdoor advertising. He serves on the board of a state trade association.

[b]Dana Vosberg[/b] joined the Group in 2017 and is responsible for finance, treasury, lender reporting and the Real Estate Optimisation Program. She previously served as Vice President, Finance at a multi-site healthcare services operator.

[b]Preston Amell[/b] leads revenue, ad operations and the Group's programmatic partnerships. He joined in 2019 from a demand-side platform, where he ran mid-market sales. He has held revenue leadership roles in local media since 2006, beginning in circulation.

[b]Kim Redditt[/b] leads Content Operations, including production, intake, categorisation and the corrections queue. She joined the Group in October 2025 from a national customer-experience outsourcing provider, where she led a 900-seat delivery organisation across three sites.

[b]Trevor Oyelaran[/b] is responsible for the Group's publishing platform, taxonomy, distribution and search performance. He joined in 2018 and led the platform build and the portfolio-wide transition completed in 2024.

[b]Susan Hatchell[/b] advises on transactions, licensing, public-notice compliance and pre-publication matters. She joined Halloran Communications in 2014 and continued with the Group following the 2016 acquisition.

Operating group leads are accountable for revenue, published item volume and cost per item within their group. They do not have content authority; content standards are set centrally. See [url=/standards]Content Standards[/url].

The Group has not maintained a separate biography page for operating group leads since 2023.
